scope: Initial read-only maintenance/workflow review followed by explicitly authorized structure-guard and focused standard-library regression fixes. No browser, branch, workflow, immutable-source or historical-evidence changes by this agent.

ciIntegration.nodeTests: npm run build invokes prebuild npm test, strict TypeScript and Vite
ciIntegration.assetAndStructureChecks: Both CI and Pages build jobs invoke npm run assets:verify, which includes the current standard-library structure guard and decoration integrity verifier
ciIntegration.browserChecks: Explicit manual/local workflows in scripts/README.md; no CI browser guarantee found

branchObservationAtStart.limitation: Read-only local-ref observation only; no fetch, deletion, live remote-branch guarantee or publication assertion. Root handles remote checks and cleanup.

findings.title: Optimized Python turns a failed structure report into successful process exit
findings.reproduction: Synthetic README contains [missing](missing.md). Normal Python exits 1/status failed; python -O exits 0/status failed because the final assert is removed.
findings.presentImpact: Current workflows do not explicitly enable optimized Python, so no current CI bypass is asserted.
findings.minimalFix: Replace the final assert with explicit nonzero SystemExit on failure; add a small standard-library subprocess regression for normal and -O execution.
findings.remediationStatus: fixed and covered by isolated CLI regressions

findings.title: Regex misses reference-style links and treats code examples as real links
findings.reproduction: [missing][target] plus [target]: missing.md returns passed; an inline-code example `[missing](missing.md)` returns failed.
findings.presentImpact: No reference-style definitions were found in current repository Markdown during this review; no current broken live documentation link is asserted.
findings.minimalFix: Either explicitly narrow the documented guard to inline-link syntax, or add limited reference-definition handling and skip inline/fenced code with targeted parser fixture regressions. Preserve frozen-reference hash and exceptions.
findings.remediationStatus: fixed and covered by isolated CLI regressions

findings.title: Stray tracked bytecode outside __pycache__ is not covered by the temporary-output boundary
findings.reproduction: A staged root stray-cache.pyc in the disposable fixture returns passed with no trackedTemporaryOutputs.
findings.presentImpact: No such file is currently tracked in the website checkout.
findings.minimalFix: Include .pyc/.pyo suffixes in the boundary (and ignore patterns if desired), retaining deliberately tracked audit logs/images and immutable originals.
findings.remediationStatus: fixed and covered by isolated CLI regressions

findings.title: Configured Actions target deprecated Node20 and are forced onto Node24 by GitHub
findings.evidence: Official successful baseline check annotations explicitly name checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, configure-pages@v5, nested upload-artifact@v4, and deploy-pages@v4. Application node-version:24 does not change action runtime.
findings.minimalFix: When workflow permission is confirmed, review and update official Actions to compatible supported releases, retaining current PR checks, Pages permissions, base paths and deploy behavior; verify required runner versions and migration notes. Do not change workflows without AGENTS-required permission.
findings.noFailureClaim: Observed baseline build/deploy checks concluded success; latest releases alone are not vulnerability evidence.
findings.remediationStatus: open; workflow permission not confirmed, no workflow change attempted

annotations.message: Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v4, actions/configure-pages@v5, actions/setup-node@v4, actions/upload-artifact@v4. For more information see: https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners/
"The ubuntu-latest label will migrate to Ubuntu 26 beginning October 19, 2026. For more information, see https://github.com/actions/runner-images/issues/14748"

retainedBoundaries: No original source or historical evidence moved, overwritten or deleted
Seven known frozen-reference link exceptions remain explicit and hash-pinned
External URLs, Markdown fragments, security properties, complete CommonMark parsing and live hosting behavior are outside the structure guard
No assertion that a newer Action release by itself is necessary for correctness or proof of current compromise

initialStructureGuardResult.scope: Relative Markdown target existence and tracked output boundaries; no external URL, fragment, security or browser assertions.

currentStructureGuardResult.scope: Supported inline/reference Markdown target existence outside fenced/inline code and tracked output boundaries; limited parser, no CommonMark conformance, external URL, fragment, security or browser assertions.

changes: Explicit process return code is preserved under Python -O/PYTHONOPTIMIZE
Limited inline/full/collapsed/shortcut reference target parsing, outside fenced blocks and inline code spans
Tracked .pyc/.pyo suffixes are rejected outside __pycache__ too; historical audit logs remain allowed
Malformed URL-shaped destinations produce a failed JSON report rather than an unstructured parser crash
authorizedRemediation.fixtureIsolation: Each regression runs the actual copied guard CLI in a disposable local Git repository; original frozen README bytes copied unchanged. No network, browser or real repository index/branch changes.
authorizedRemediation.diffCheck: git diff --check on the two implementation files passed
authorizedRemediation.parserScope: Inline destinations and same-line reference definitions with full/collapsed/shortcut usage, case/whitespace labels, fenced and inline code. Does not claim full CommonMark semantics; indented code, raw HTML, complex nested labels/destinations and external/fragment validation remain outside scope.

workflowPermissionState: Not confirmed by this child. AGENTS requires workflow permission; no workflow edits attempted. Root handles any permission verification and publication.
